meta_jurisdiction_context.sovereign_country_en: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

UK-Gibraltar FATCA-style Intergovernmental Agreement for the Exchange of Information (2014)

EU-Gibraltar post-Brexit Treaty on Security and Cooperation (2021) — prudential and AML cooperation perimeter

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime Act 2015 (Gibraltar), as amended; Financial Services Act 2019; Limited Partnerships Act 2019 (Cap. 324); Companies Act 2014 (Cap. 102); Beneficial Ownership (Access to Facilitate Compliance with FATF Objectives) Regulations 2017; Sanctions Act 2019 and Sanctions Regulations 2020; GFSC AML/CFT Guidance Notes (2023 Edition); MONEYVAL and FATF Recommendations as transposed.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, Gibraltar / Companies House Gibraltar

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory initial and continuous screening of all UBOs, general partners, fund contributors, and authorised signatories against: (i) OFAC SDN List and Sectoral Sanctions Identifications; (ii) UN Consolidated Security Council Sanctions; (iii) UK OFSI Consolidated List; (iv) Gibraltar domestic sanctions designations under the Sanctions Act 2019; (v) FATF High-Risk and Non-Cooperative Jurisdictions List; (vi) EU post-Brexit retained restrictive measures applicable to Gibraltar. Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) is mandatory where a PEP holds at least 25% ownership or where the business originates traffic from a High-Risk Third Country. Screening is refreshed within 72 hours prior to any change in partners and at minimum on a rolling 72-hour cycle after incorporation; source of wealth documentation is secured for any PEP-linked funding above USD 50,000.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Gibraltar Companies House online portal (companieshouse.gi) and GFSC Companies e-Filing System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: English statutory register only; names must be expressed in Latin-script English characters. The ELP name must contain the statutory descriptor 'Limited Partnership', 'LP', or 'L.P.'. Arabic numerals and conventional punctuation (period, comma, ampersand) are accepted; non-Roman scripts, diacritics, and transliterated characters are not accepted for registration.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection under Companies Act 2014, s.7(3), the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the Registrar of Companies within 21 days of the rejection notice, attaching a memorandum of grounds and, where applicable, the ministerial or regulatory consent previously obtained. If the Registrar issues a final adverse determination, the applicant may petition the Minister responsible for Financial Services within a further 14 days. A final judicial remedy is available via an application for judicial review in the Supreme Court of Gibraltar, which must be lodged within 3 months of the final administrative decision. A single 30-day extension of the name reservation may be requested online before expiry upon payment of the statutory renewal fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted at formation only where provided by a GFSC-licensed corporate services provider and consisting of a physical, serviceable registered office address in Gibraltar (never a P.O. Box). For a real-time video matching social app under ISIC 6311 with Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML classification and planned Apple IAP/Paymentwall rails, a pure virtual mailbox satisfies the statutory registered-office mandate but will fail OECD/G20 BEPS Action 5 economic substance expectations and will likely be rejected by prospective UK-Gibraltar EMIs and correspondent banks. A serviced physical office with at least one in-country director or qualified executive is the recommended commercial-substance benchmark.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 25% annualised likelihood of an unannounced physical inspection by the GFSC/Registrar investigations unit during the first operating year for a medium-risk digital platform; likelihood rises to approximately 60% if the entity later applies for a Gibraltar EMI, payments, or DLT licence.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Limited Partnerships Act 2019 (Gibraltar), ss. 3, 6–11; Limited Partnerships Regulations 2020, Reg. 5; Companies Act 2014 (Gibraltar) s. 190 (foreign limited partnership recognition); Income Tax Act 2010 (Gibraltar), s. 8 and Sixth Schedule (pass-through treatment of exempt partnerships)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Gibraltar Companies House, Registry of Limited Partnerships, 3rd Floor, 57A Line Wall Road, Gibraltar GX11 1AA
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form LP-1 — Statement of Registration of a Limited Partnership together with the Statutory Declaration of Compliance (first General Partner)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an Exempted Limited Partnership; capital contributions are governed by the Limited Partnership Agreement (LPA) and may be cash or in-kind; no escrow account requirement is imposed, but the contributed capital must be received within 30 days of the certificate of registration to satisfy the statutory declaration on solvency.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) That the General Partner approves the Limited Partnership Agreement of the Exempted Limited Partnership in the form tabled, and the Partnership is hereby constituted under the Limited Partnerships Act 2019 (Gibraltar). (2) That the initial capital contributions and admission of the Limited Partners in Schedule A are ratified. (3) That the registered office shall be at Suite 5, 57A Line Wall Road, Gibraltar, and the Company Secretary is appointed. (4) That Nominee Ltd is appointed first General Partner and BDO Gibraltar Ltd is appointed Administrator. (5) That the AML Compliance Officer, Money Laundering Reporting Officer, and bank mandate signatories are approved and authorised to execute and file Form LP-1 and all necessary declarations. Signed by the General Partner.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies House — Name Reservation Desk (online portal: www.csra.gi)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a reserved name application for the proposed ELP, ensuring the name ends with 'Limited Partnership' or 'L.P.'. The Registrar checks conflicts with existing registered names and prohibited words. Upon approval, the name is reserved for 90 days. Payment of the GBP 10 reservation fee is made online.
required_dossiers: Completed Name Reservation Form (NR-1)
Proposed identity of first General Partner (Certified Passport copy)
Proof of registered agent appointment letter
Payment confirmation of reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused due to similarity or a prohibited word, the applicant may file a revised name within 14 days without an additional fee, or appeal to the Registrar under the Business Names (Gibraltar) Regulations within 21 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the Limited Partnership Agreement and statutory declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notarial Officer / Authorised Gibraltar legal counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Gibraltar-licensed lawyer to draft the LPA containing the capital structure, profit-sharing ratios, management powers of the General Partner, and transfer provisions. The General Partner and each Limited Partner execute the LPA; the General Partner also signs a statutory declaration confirming compliance with the Limited Partnerships Act 2019.
required_dossiers: Limited Partnership Agreement (signed by all partners)
Statutory Declaration of Compliance (Form LP-1 Annex B)
Certified copies of passport and proof of residential address for each partner
Registered office consent letter from the Gibraltar-licensed administrator
AML/KYC source-of-funds documentation for each beneficial owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the Registrar queries deficient notarisation or incomplete counterparty KYC, corrected documents may be re-submitted within 10 working days; missing evidence of the registered office consent is typically curable by fresh consent letter, failing which a new declaration fee applies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Form LP-1 and issuance of the certificate of registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies House — Registry of Limited Partnerships
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed Form LP-1 together with the statutory declaration and the approved name reservation. Payment of the GBP 95 government registration fee (approx. USD 120) is made via the Companies House electronic filing interface. Upon validation, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Registration and the ELP obtains separate legal personality.
required_dossiers: Form LP-1 (Statement of Registration)
Statutory Declaration of Compliance
Certified copy of the Limited Partnership Agreement
Name reservation certificate
Registered office address confirmation (Form LP-2)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is challenged, the Registrar issues a Notice of Defect specifying omissions. The applicant has 10 working days to cure; re-filing after expiry requires a fresh declaration and a GBP 30 late-cure surcharge.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax status confirmation and Economic Substance registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Commissioner of Income Tax — Tax Treatment Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Certificate of Registration to the Commissioner together with Form EST-1 to confirm the ELP's pass-through classification and non-resident status. As an offshore-exempted structure, the ELP applies for confirmation that its income derived outside Gibraltar is not chargeable to Gibraltar tax. The application is administered jointly with the Companies House Economic Substance filing requirement.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration (Form LP-1 issued copy)
Form EST-1 (Tax Status Election)
LPA and capital contribution schedule
Declaration of non-Gibraltar-resident participation
Proof of registered agent (Tax Representative) appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the Commissioner requests further evidence of economic substance or the non-Gibraltar source of income, the applicant may file a supplementary statement within 30 days; an appeal against a refusal lies to the Income Tax Review Board within 30 days of the notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) / Gibraltar Regulatory Authority (GRA) — Data Protection Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the ELP as a 'relevant person' under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2015 (Gibraltar) if it carries on any financial or crypto-asset activity, and file the Data Protection Act 2004 registration as a data controller with the GRA. The General Partner must appoint a licensed Compliance Officer, MLRO, and a Data Protection Officer. The video-matching platform's processing of user personal data must be stated in the registration annex.
required_dossiers: GFSC Relevant Person Registration form (if applicable)
GRA Data Controller Registration (Form DC-1)
AML Policy and Risk Assessment (Medium-Risk Enhanced tier)
Appointment letters for MLRO, Compliance Officer, and DPO
Privacy Policy and lawful-basis consent wording
Business continuity statement for video-streaming infrastructure
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Deficient privacy or AML documentation is addressable through the GRA's 15-working-day correction window; repeat non-compliance attracts a fine under the Data Protection Act 2004 s. 65, but no licence lapse is triggered before the cure period ends.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Banking / EMI account opening and post-formation filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar-licensed banks or UK/Gibraltar Electronic Money Institutions (e.g. reputable EMI partners)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open an operating account in the ELP's name, presenting the Certificate of Registration, tax status confirmation, and the partnership onboarding pack. Execute the banking mandate listing authorised signatories. The payment rails for this venture (Apple IAP and Paymentwall) are established and the EMI's compliance team performs a medium-risk enhanced due-diligence review.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration and tax confirmation letters
Certified copies of all partners' passports and proof of address
Signed banking mandate and resolution of the General Partner
LPA and beneficial ownership register (PSC Register)
Funds source and business plan supporting the video-match platform
Executed EMI merchant agreement covering Apple IAP and Paymentwall settlement flows
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the bank raises requests for further information, the General Partner must provide enhanced KYC within 20 working days; refusal of the application results in a right to re-apply with a second EMI bank, and the ELP may escalate to the GFSC Ombudsman for service failures under the Banking (Complaints) Regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Gibraltar Regulatory Authority (GRA) — Digital Services and Data Protection Unit (jointly with the Department of Commerce for e-commerce notifications)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Data Controller Registration Certificate under the Data Protection Act 2004 and Digital Service Provider Notification under the Electronic Commerce (Gibraltar) Regulations 2002

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of the Environment, Sustainability and Climate Change (Gibraltar)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no EIA required; the undertaking is a pure digital service company with no physical manufacturing installation, no combustion plant, and no discharge points
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero direct point-source discharges; the ELP must comply with the Waste (Gibraltar) Regulations 2000 for e-waste disposal of server hardware, the Restriction of Hazardous Substances Directive (RoHS) for procured equipment, and the Carbon Reduction Commitment Code for office premises; all cloud infrastructure must be hosted in Tier III or higher data centres with PUE certification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not physically applicable to the digital business; however, the Gibraltar Civil Contingencies Authority and the Ministry of Business issue a fire-safety certificate for the registered office, a workplace inspection clearance under the Health and Safety at Work Act (Gibraltar), and a business continuity certificate for the head-office premises. The platform's production infrastructure must maintain ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type II certification for resilience and occupational data security.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Commissioner of Income Tax, HM Government of Gibraltar – Income Tax Office, 6-8 Harbourside, Gibraltar; official portal: www.gibraltar.gov.gi/income-tax
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: An Exempted Limited Partnership (ELP) incorporated in Gibraltar must apply to the Registrar of Companies for registration under the Limited Partnerships Act and obtain a Certificate of Registration; thereafter the ELP must register with the Income Tax Office for a Gibraltar Tax Identification Number (TIN/TRN). The application requires: (i) certificate of registration of the ELP; (ii) deed of partnership or limited partnership agreement; (iii) full particulars of all general and limited partners (name, address, jurisdiction of residence and tax residence); (iv) registered office address in Gibraltar; and (v) application form IR1 (or equivalent). No VAT ID is available because Gibraltar is not part of the EU VAT area.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible: the ELP is fiscally transparent under Gibraltar Income Tax Act 2010; the partnership itself is not chargeable to income tax; partners are taxable in their own hands. Non-resident partners are within territorial scope only if they carry on a trade in Gibraltar through a permanent establishment; otherwise they are not subject to Gibraltar tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: There is no check-the-box regime in Gibraltar; pass-through treatment is the statutory default. An ELP may nevertheless apply for an Exempt Limited Partnership certificate under s.74 Limited Partnerships Act, which provides certainty that the partnership is treated as transparent and not as a separate taxable unit. For hybrid mismatch purposes, the Taxes (Hybrid Mismatch) Regulations 2019 apply; a partner may file a formal transparency election with the Commissioner to align the Gibraltar treatment with the jurisdiction of any partner where the partnership is treated as opaque there.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Not applicable (Gibraltar has no VAT/GST/sales or use tax; excise and import duties apply to physical goods under the Customs Ordinance 2016)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No VAT/GST registration threshold exists in Gibraltar. A person importing taxable goods may require customs-warehouse or importer registration with HM Customs (Gibraltar) regardless of value; service suppliers are not required to register for indirect tax because no indirect tax is levied on services in Gibraltar.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, e-invoicing or digital stamping mandate in force. Commercial invoices issued in accordance with the Companies Act and Income Tax (Record Keeping) Rules satisfy compliance. If physical goods are imported/exported, the HM Customs Single Administrative Document declaration is filed electronically via customs clearance systems.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable: exports of goods and offshore services from Gibraltar are wholly outside the scope of Gibraltar indirect tax because there is no VAT or GST. Consequently there is no zero-rating regime to claim. Suppliers are not required to substantiate zero-rating refunds; however, to evidence non-establishment and export status for foreign regulators, the supplier should retain the customary export documents.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: In the absence of VAT/GST, there is no export VAT clawback; however, false or misleading customs declarations, or arrangements contrived to obtain a fiscal advantage, may be investigated by the Commissioner and HM Customs. Penalties include fines up to £10,000 or 200% of the duty evaded, criminal liability, and for tax matters retrospective adjustments for up to 6 years (unlimited period in cases of fraud). In addition, treaty abuse and permanent establishment reconstruction may give rise to partner-level tax assessments with clawback of any foreign tax credits erroneously claimed.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC); there is no independent Central Bank of Gibraltar – the Government of Gibraltar issues local currency notes under the Currency Notes Act 2011, and the UK's HM Treasury retains ultimate monetary authority. The Gibraltar pound (GIP) is pegged at parity with GBP.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The GIP is unconditionally convertible into GBP at parity. Gibraltar maintains no foreign-exchange controls or approval mechanisms on either current account or capital account transactions. A Cayman Islands Exempted Limited Partnership (KY_ELP) may freely inject capital, receive revenue in USD/GBP/EUR, and remit profits to non-resident partners without any convertibility barrier. No exchange control approval is required for profit distribution, loan repayment, or capital repatriation, and Gibraltar imposes no withholding tax on distributions to non-resident partners under its territorial tax system.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Gibraltar imposes no statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds, no minimum conversion ratio, and no timeline within which export or digital-service receipts must be repatriated or converted into local currency. Inbound USD proceeds from Apple IAP and Paymentwall settlement may be retained in foreign currency indefinitely.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate-to-High. A Gibraltar-licensed Electronic Money Institution (EMI), regulated by the GFSC under the Financial Services (Electronic Money) Regulations 2011, may offer multi-currency virtual IBANs and faster payment rails to a KY_ELP without requiring full commercial bank relationship. However, offshore EMIs incorporated outside Gibraltar cannot passport into Gibraltar post-Brexit; a GFSC-authorised EMI or a UK/EEA EMI with GFSC reverse recognition is required. The GFSC will apply enhanced due diligence because the ELP is a Cayman vehicle, and will require evidence of economic substance, source of funds, and the app's transactional monitoring framework.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership with non-resident partners, most Gibraltar tier-1 commercial banks mandate a physical presence of the general partner's senior manager or the ultimate beneficial owner for the first onboarding interview. Remote opening is permitted only under GFSC guidance via a regulated introducer or notary, with a live video KYC interview and independent verification of identification documents. Some private banks (e.g., Turicum) may waive in-person appearance if the ELP already holds a relationship with a reputable GFSC-licensed corporate services provider.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The video-matching app enables anonymous user-to-user interaction with high-velocity micropayments and virtual gift incentives, raising typologies for money laundering, sanctions evasion, and consumer harm.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A documented KYC/CDD policy covering all merchants/payout recipients, transaction monitoring rules, device fingerprinting, red-flag scenarios for virtual currency exchanges and churning, plus a GFSC-compliant AML/CFT risk assessment and independent audit report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The ELP's ultimate beneficial owners are non-resident and lack meaningful economic substance in Gibraltar beyond a registered agent and virtual office.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The ELP's economic substance file evidencing core income-generating activities performed in Gibraltar: board meeting minutes, compliance function mandates, payroll records for local staff, a physical lease for the principal place of business, and a computing policy showing treasury and risk management decisions taken in Gibraltar.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound payments to geographically dispersed content moderators and partner studios lack auditable commercial purpose.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master service agreements with each counterparty, beneficial-ownership disclosures for corporate counterparties, time-stamped work logs, monthly payout reconciliations, and tax documentation (W-8BEN-E/W-9, CRS declarations, and EU DAC6 cross-border arrangements where relevant).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cayman ELP structure may be perceived as an opaque offshore arrangement designed to conceal the ultimate source of funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the ELP's certificate of limited partnership, register of members, exempted status certificate, notarised declarations of source of wealth and funds from each partner/beneficial owner, and a fund-flow diagram showing the capital injection path from the founding investors.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections are executed through SWIFT MT103 wire transfers from the investor's bank to the ELP's Gibraltar-licensed bank account. The SWIFT purpose code should be 'CAPT' (Capital Transfer) or 'EQUI' (Equity) with a narrative referencing 'KY_ELP capital account contribution pursuant to LPA section [X]'. For GBP funding, the ELP may receive via CHAPS or Faster Payments if the source bank is UK-based; for USD, settlement occurs via Fedwire/CHIPS. The receiving bank will require a copy of the executed contribution schedule, the ELP's revised capital account statement, and a valid LEI if the transfer exceeds 100,000 USD.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary clearing rail for outbound disbursements is SWIFT MT103 (single customer credit transfer). For recurring service payments to EU/EEA developers and content partners, SEPA Credit Transfers are used through the Gibraltar bank's SEPA participation. UK-domiciled suppliers are paid via CHAPS or Faster Payments. Commercial letters of credit under ICC UCP 600 are not typical for digital services, but can be structured for IP licensing or significant technology procurement, using the Gibraltar bank's trade finance desk; MT700/MT710 issuances and swift advice are supported.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla FX forwards between USD, GBP, and EUR executed under an ISDA Master Agreement with a GFSC-licensed counterparty or an OECD-domiciled global bank
FX swaps (simultaneous spot and forward exchange of principal amounts) for liquidity management across the ELP's settlement currencies
Cross-currency swaps to hedge the USD-receipt / GBP-payment operating mismatch, with ISDA documentation and credit support annex

Deliverable GBP/USD forwards (preferred over NDFs because GIP is fully convertible and pegged 1:1 to GBP, making non-deliverable instruments redundant and therefore impermissible under GFSC product intervention rules)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return / Confirmation Statement of an Exempted Limited Partnership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Her Majesty's Government of Gibraltar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after the anniversary of the formation date of the ELP
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of up to GIP 1,200 per event; continued default for 3 successive years exposes the ELP to administrative strike-off from the Gibraltar Register of Companies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March following the tax year ending 31 December (extension not automatic)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late return penalties up to GIP 1,800 plus daily default fines; the Commissioner may estimate assessment and enforce recovery against partnership assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Financial Services Commission / Registrar of Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the ELP's annual confirmation date, normally within 42 days after the anniversary of registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to confirm or update beneficial ownership data attracts fixed penalties up to GIP 500 per breach and potential criminal fines for partners; persistent default may lead to registry strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Internal Statutory Register Audit and Minute Book Review
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered office / licensed corporate service provider (internal compliance; no regulator filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Performed annually in alignment with the ELP's financial year end and before the Annual Return is submitted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct government penalty for the internal audit; however, failure to maintain accurate registers on site is an offence under the Gibraltar Companies Act and renders the ELP liable to daily fines and director/partner disqualification actions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent audit is required if the ELP exceeds two of the following in the relevant financial year: turnover above GIP 10.2 million, balance sheet total above GIP 5.1 million, average employees above 50; an audit is also compulsory if any partner is a body corporate or if partners holding at least 10% of profit-sharing rights request one in writing.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted by the European Union and applied in Gibraltar for large entities; small entities may use Gibraltar Financial Reporting Standard FRS 102 consistent with UK GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The general partner must review the beneficial ownership register on an annual basis and file a written confirmation alongside the Annual Return stating that the register is accurate and complete. Every transfer of a partnership interest or change in beneficial ownership must be recorded in the UBO register before the next annual confirmation date; failure to disclose a qualifying change within 14 days of becoming known is an offence subject to a penalty of GIP 500.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Consent and Resignation Records for Corporate Partners

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $1,200 - $3,500 depending on regulated trust and corporate service provider
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $4,000 - $8,500 for a medium-risk digital services ELP using IFRS accounts

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 12.5% (standard Gibraltar corporate income tax rate; the Exempted Limited Partnership itself is fiscally transparent, and each corporate partner is taxable at 12.5% on its allocable profit share).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays, no patent-box preferential rate, and no investment allowance moratorium are currently in force for ISIC 6311 application providers. The ELP is not itself a preferential vehicle; it is a pass-through arrangement. Ordinary deductible expenditure includes personnel costs, leased premises, cloud infrastructure, payment-processing fees, and amortisation of capitalized software. Unrelieved trading losses may be carried forward against future profits for a maximum of 5 years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Gibraltar Annual Partnership Income Tax Return (Form GP-ELP) filed electronically through the Gibraltar Income Tax Office 'eTax' portal. For a non-resident ELP, the return is accompanied by a Non-Resident Partner Schedule (Schedule NRP) allocating Gibraltar-source profits to each partner.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: On or before 30 November following the fiscal year-end (Gibraltar tax year aligns to 31 December; a specially approved accounting year may be used for the ELP, with the return due no later than 9 months after the approved year-end).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: ELP registered name, registration number, registered office in Gibraltar, Gibraltar tax reference, UK TIN if claiming DTA relief, and foreign tax identifier of each general and limited partner.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident limited partners must enter their jurisdiction tax reference, country code, and, where applicable, a UK or Gibraltar treaty certificate. If no Gibraltar-source profits are reported, the Schedule NRP must still be annexed with a declaration that the ELP is not carrying on a trade through a Gibraltar permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Approved accounting period, turnover, deductible operating expenses, capital allowances claimed, and chargeable profits computed under the Gibraltar Income Tax Act.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident partners, only the share arising from Gibraltar operations or the Gibraltar permanent establishment of the ELP is entered. Foreign-source income allocated but not received or derived through Gibraltar must be excluded and shown in the reconciliation schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of cross-border transactions with connected persons: consideration paid, arm’s-length adjustment, transfer-pricing methodology selected, and the legal written agreement governing each controlled transaction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must certify that the ELP maintains a Gibraltar-local transfer-pricing file for all controlled transactions exceeding GBP 2 million in aggregate, including royalty payments to the technology licensor and payment-facilitator service charges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 — Profit Allocation and Beneficial Owners
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit-sharing percentages and amounts distributable to each partner, including details of any special allocations, carried-interest arrangements, or loans of the ELP that may recharacterise reserves as book debt.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Every non-resident partner, including an intermediate Cayman Islands ELP or trust, must name its ultimate beneficial owner and file a KYC schedule. Failure to disclose the natural-person owner cancels treaty benefits and exposes the Gibraltar general partner to compliance penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an initial penalty of GBP 200 plus a daily surcharge of GBP 40 per day, capped at GBP 3,600 per return. In addition, the Comptroller may issue a determination based on estimated profits and impose a further penalty of up to 100% of the tax under-assessed for failure to produce records. Deliberate withholding of a return after written notice is treated as tax evasion and referred to the Gibraltar Attorney General for criminal prosecution.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% — Gibraltar imposes no corporate withholding tax on dividends, profit distributions, or dissolution proceeds of an ELP. Because the ELP is transparent, distributions are treated as tax-free returns of capital or previously taxed profits.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Where the recipient asserts reduced or zero withholding in a foreign source state, the Gibraltar Income Tax Office issues a Gibraltar Tax Residency and Treaty Entitlement Certificate (Form TRC-GI) after confirming the ELP has economic substance and the ultimate owner is resident in the treaty jurisdiction. The applicant submits the TRC, a Form WHT-REBATE Declaration, and a certified profit allocation statement to the foreign paying agent prior to remittance, or before the foreign filing deadline to obtain a refund under the UK-Gibraltar DTA provisions and the OECD Multilateral Instrument relationship. The application must include evidence of beneficial ownership, absence of back-to-back conduit arrangements, and prior-year substantiated economic activity.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Gibraltar domestic statutory rate is 0% on outbound royalties and debt interest paid by a Gibraltar company/partnership to non-residents, provided the expenditure is incurred for taxable business operations. Under applicable treaty arrangements, the maximum source-state rate for qualifying royalties and interest is generally 0%; however, the counterparty state may impose rates up to 10% for royalties and 10% for interest where no treaty or improper-conduit protection exists, and in such cases the Irish/UK sub-processing payer must withhold in accordance with local law and the Gibraltar entity may file a foreign tax credit claim in Gibraltar, subject to the 5-year carryforward constraint.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: GBP 2 million aggregate controlled transaction value per fiscal year, or GBP 1 million for intangible-related payments such as software licensing royalties, triggers mandatory Gibraltar Master File and Local File contemporaneous documentation. A Country-by-Country reporting obligation arises for an ultimate parent group with consolidated revenue above EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Gibraltar Economic Substance (Companies and Partnerships) Regulations 2019 apply. The ISIC 6311 video-match operation is assessed as a 'distribution and service centre business' or 'IP business' if brand/software value is stored in Gibraltar. If a relevant activity is carried out, the ELP must prove: (a) management decisions are taken in Gibraltar, (b) full-time employees and physical premises are adequate, (c) core income-generating activities — server administration, user-onboarding, and cross-border payment routing — are performed in Gibraltar, and (d) the ELP is not a shell, mailbox, or conduit. A non-resident ELP engaged solely in passive investment may be treated as a pure equity holding company with a reduced substance test.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Arranging the ELP to route video-chat transaction revenue through the Gibraltar partnership while directing all management decisions, employees, and operational control from the UK, thereby establishing a hidden UK permanent establishment; understating Gibraltar-source sales by recording them through unlicensed Paymentwall/IAP settlement accounts not disclosed on the tax return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil fraud penalties of up to 200% of the unpaid tax; interest at 8% per annum compounded; seizure of operating bank accounts; disqualification of the audit sponsor; criminal fine of GBP 100,000 and up to 7 years’ imprisonment under the Income Tax Act (Gibraltar).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The Inland Revenue may pierce the ELP veil where the general partner acts as a façade and the UK directors personally operate the app; directors become jointly and severally liable for the entire tax undercharge, face travel bans under the Income Tax (Enforcement) Regulations, and in aggravated cases receive custodial sentence of up to 7 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Submitting a Schedule NRP that allocates 100% of profits to a foreign partner — commonly a Cayman Islands ELP — while the Gibraltar bank mandate is operated by UK residents and the randoms video-match service carries on commercial activity through an undisclosed Gibraltar office.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recomputation of profit against the Gibraltar general partner; increased liability at 12.5% plus late payment interest; financial penalty of GBP 10,000 per false declaration; referral to the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission for administrative revocation and the issuance of a 'Red Alert' for money-laundering.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The court may treat the ELP as the alter ego of the controlling UK board, making unpaid corporate tax a personal debt; directors cannot leave Gibraltar while assessment under appeal; intentional concealment carries imprisonment of up to 5 years and an order prohibiting them from acting as a director without prior court consent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Gibraltar arm has no office, no dedicated social-telephony employees, and board minutes signed retroactively, while the app’s server logs, data-science staff, and user-match algorithm decisions reside in the UK or in a third-country innovation hub; no audited Core Income Generating Activity ledger is maintained.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Removal of Gibraltar tax residence by the Commissioner; imposition of a penalty equal to 20% of gross profit attributable to the relevant activity; notification to the UK HMRC under the exchange-of-information framework; cost-recovery surcharge of GBP 50,000 for administrative investigation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who certify false economic substance declarations commit offences under the Economic Substance Regulations and may be fined up to GBP 15,000 and imprisoned for 3 years; where the company is deemed to be UK resident, UK director disqualification orders and extradition to the UK may also be pursued.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging excessive management fees to the Gibraltar video-app enterprise for 'algorithm licensing' from a shell company in a zero-tax jurisdiction, or paying Paymentwall/IAP charges at a percentage materially above independent comparables; failing to file the Master File/Local File within 30 days of the tax return despite the GBP 2 million threshold being crossed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary adjustment restating taxable profits at the 12.5% Gibraltar rate; secondary adjustments treated as additional distributions subject to no WHT but reclassified as capital; penalty of 40% of the avoided tax amount; denial of treaty relief for the related-party royalty flow.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legislation attributes responsibility for the ELP’s controlled documentation to the general partner’s board; directors knowingly signing distorted TP returns are civilly liable for the full excess tax plus 10% interest, and may be subject to a 4-year travel restriction barring offshore personal spending allocation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using Apple IAP and Paymentwall settlement accounts to receive video-match user funds while circumventing the ELP’s Gibraltar bank account, with no Source of Wealth file for the ultimate beneficiary; processing users with crypto-funded prepaid cards and failing to file Suspicious Activity Reports; wiring residual profits within 48 hours to a UAE personal account.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Proceeds of Crime (Gibraltar) Act penalties of up to GBP 250,000 or 14 years’ imprisonment per transaction; money-laundering reporting fine of GBP 100,000; suspension of the ELP’s external payment reconciliation licence; freezing orders over all worldwide payment processing accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally accountable under AML obligations as statutory 'relevant persons'; culpability includes imprisonment of 14 years, confiscation orders over app revenues, overseas travel bans, and extradition to the United Kingdom; the general partner may be personally sued for third-party merchant-funding losses.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Beneficial Ownership Non-Disclosure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The collaboration agreement and the app’s user terms are signed by a nominee general partner; no natural-person partner appears on the disclosed register; equity in the parent entity is represented by bearer certificates or discretionary interests; the chargeable profits are repatriated to a trust that has no commercial link to the video-match business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalties of GBP 100,000 for failure to maintain a natural-person beneficial ownership register in Gibraltar; the Registrar may strike off the ELP and require the general partner to assign profits to the Crown after 3 months; aggravated facts are reported to the Gibraltar Police Financial Intelligence Unit as a shell-company predicate offence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts in Gibraltar and the UK are prepared to pierce the veil where the ELP is merely a façade for the UK founders; directors and the nominee general partner become jointly liable for all commercial debts of the app, lose any cap on liability under the limited partnership agreement, and may be jailed for up to 10 years for conspiracy to fabricate ownership.
